elements.evidence: The added language expressly permits Customer to terminate the Agreement or any Order Form for convenience.

elements.element: Customer's termination-for-convenience right is exercisable on 30 days' prior notice.
elements.evidence: The clause requires 30 days' prior notice to Vendor.

elements.element: Customer's termination-for-convenience notice must be written.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly requires prior written notice.

elements.element: Vendor must provide a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees following Customer's termination for convenience.
elements.evidence: Vendor must refund prepaid Fees attributable to the period after the effective termination date, which implements a pro-rata refund.

elements.element: Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly states that Vendor has no right to terminate the Agreement or any Order Form for convenience during a committed term.
The added language expressly grants Customer a termination-for-convenience right.

elements.element: Customer's termination-for-convenience right is exercisable on 60–90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The clause specifies 30 days' notice, which is outside the fallback range of 60–90 days.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee imposed on Customer must not exceed three months' fees.
elements.evidence: The clause imposes no early-termination fee, so the operative fee under this language is zero and does not exceed three months' fees.

elements.element: Any Vendor termination for convenience may take effect only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: The clause bars Vendor termination for convenience during a committed term but does not expressly limit any such termination to taking effect only at the end of a term.

elements.element: Vendor must give 90 days' notice of any permitted termination for convenience.
elements.evidence: No 90-day notice requirement applies to Vendor.

result.reason: The redline cleanly adds every preferred protection while preserving the existing cause-based termination rights. It does not independently satisfy the fallback because Customer's notice period is 30 rather than 60–90 days and it does not provide the fallback's end-of-term/90-day framework for any Vendor convenience termination.
